transitions.authority: endpoint (§15.3 step 1): the authority endpoint's own serializable SQL transaction, revalidating dependencies against the observed journal head — internal mutation protocol, never a callable BPP operation
transitions.notes: A competing CAS advanced the head: complete dependency revalidation under a new proposed generation; the old pending transition stays inert (§15.3 crash semantics).

transitions.authority: witness (§15.3 step 2): the external non-rollbackable journal facility compare-and-swapping (incarnation, prior generation, prior digest) to the exact next AuthorityJournalEntry — internal mutation protocol, never a callable BPP operation
transitions.notes: Returns a signed AuthorityJournalReceipt; the transaction id and transition digest make the CAS retry/query-safe — a re-sent request for an already-journaled transaction returns the existing receipt, never a second entry (§15.3).

transitions.authority: witness (§15.3 step 2): the external non-rollbackable journal facility compare-and-swapping (incarnation, prior generation, prior digest) to the exact next AuthorityJournalEntry — internal mutation protocol, never a callable BPP operation
transitions.notes: A witness timeout (receipt lost in flight, request lost, or CAS lost with the response vanished) is queried by transaction id and never guessed (§15.3 crash semantics; problem kind authority_witness_unknown, §14.9).

transitions.authority: witness (§15.3 step 2): the query by transaction id against the external journal — internal mutation protocol, never a callable BPP operation
transitions.notes: The query finds the exact entry: witness success before SQL finalize is recovered by the exact receipt and finalized once (§15.3 crash semantics).

transitions.notes: Marks the exact pending set finalized/visible, advances the local journal mirror, and makes the retained result readable; only then may Byom return success, release a credential or permit, publish an event, or allow a dependent transition (§15.3). §14.8 crash outcome: every crash state follows section 15.3.
